gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the MINI 2's closest single frame (52 × 64 mm at 120 mm) covers 3,328 mm², 2.25× less area than the Seal's 100 × 75 mm frame (7,500 mm²), or that a 20 mm part spans 38% of the MINI 2's short side against 27% on the Seal. The price per detail point is also new: the Seal costs $22.70 per point across 1 mm ($454 ÷ 20) and the Seal Lite $15.05 ($215 ÷ 14.3).
standout_why: I compared against three pages. 3dprinting.com small-format (cited) lists the inputs: MINI 2 52×64 mm at 120 mm, Seal and Seal Lite 100×75 mm, point distance 0.05 / 0.07 mm, and prices of about $699 and $359. It computes no frame area, frame fill or cost per point. Maker Machines Atlas (cited) gives no field of view (FOV) and no minimum object size; its only arithmetic is an ownership range of list price plus $50–$500. CompareFoundry (cited in the third chat) gives no FOV or price and computes nothing. Print3DIndex (cited) returned 403 and I could not read it. The derivation is new, but a reader could work it out from the cited 3dprinting.com page, and that page's prices are now out of date (the Seal is $454 today, not about $699). That is why I scored it 1, not 2.
decides: It supports the MINI 2 for parts under about 30 mm: its near frame is 2.25× smaller, so a small object fills more of each frame. It supports the Seal and Seal Lite as the value picks. At today's 3DMakerpro store prices the Seal ($454) is $375 under the MINI 2 ($829), and the Seal Lite ($215) is $614 under. ChatGPT priced the Seal at $559.99 and "~$450–$700", which is wrong against the maker store today. I can't confirm or rule out the Raptor and Einstar Vega for tiny parts because I couldn't open their spec pages.
